html:
The Kukatja are an Aboriginal people of the northern edge of the Western Desert in Western Australia, south of the Kimberley, around Lake Gregory and the community of Balgo. They speak a dialect of the Western Desert language.

Their neighbours were the Walmajarri and Jaru to the north, the Ngardi and Warlpiri to the east and the Pintupi to the south. A Catholic mission opened in the area in 1939 and later settled at Balgo, where people of several desert groups came to live.

From the 1980s Balgo became a centre of the desert painting movement that began at Papunya, and Kukatja artists became widely known. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Kukatja are an Aboriginal people of the northern edge of the Western Desert in Western Australia, south of the Kimberley, around Lake Gregory and the community of Balgo. They speak a dialect of the Western Desert language.
